A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPICE and contain readable main text, equations, Figures 1–9, Tables 1–15, and Appendices A–H. The page reflow does not remove material or prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-tuning experiments on Qwen2-7B and LLaMA2-7B, gradient analyses, ablations, and additional empirical results in Appendices F and H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and the appendix analyses of selection budgets, proxy models, and computational costs.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the conflict-penalized score in Equation 14, the stopping rule in Equation 15, and the proxy-based selection procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same instruction-tuning sources and eight evaluation benchmarks. The additional dataset coverage in Appendix F and the tasks evaluated in Appendix H are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Full, Random, IFD, Fisher, LESS, SelectIT, DPP, TSDS, and LEAD as comparators. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the appendix comparisons, including Null, Fisher, and DPP in Table 14.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the 10% selection design, selecting 12 samples from pools of 120, and the same fine-tuning settings. Appendix G evaluation protocols and Appendix H budget, proxy-model, and stopping-threshold settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The penalty, proxy, update-interval, stopping-threshold, and data-budget analyses are retained. Gradient diagnostics, diversity measures, overlap and clustering analyses, training curves, and selection case studies in Appendices F and H are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repetitions for the main experiments, six for the decay analysis, and ten trials per subset size in Appendix F.4.1. Significance statements and graphical uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged across the main text and appendices. For example, Tables 1–2 retain SPICE averages of 58.0 for Qwen2-7B and 31.1 for LLaMA2-7B; the budget and timing results in Tables 14–15 also match.

T1.justification: The definitions, submodularity and curvature guarantees, perturbation bounds, and proofs in Appendices A–E are unchanged. Theorem 4's assumptions footnote is relocated and renumbered without changing its content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same theoretical contributions and claims about conflict-aware selection, information retention, and full-data-level performance using 10% of the data. The added code-access sentence does not change these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of conflict-related marginal-gain decay, bound violations in Appendix F.4, limited cross-architecture transfer, and SPICE+'s accuracy–cost tradeoff. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and a direct hyperlink to the SPICE project repository in the abstract; v1 provides no corresponding project-code link. Implementation settings, hardware disclosures, and runtime information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6, the cited works, and the positioning relative to gradient-based, information-based, and model-aware selection methods remain unchanged. The added conference header does not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds an ICLR 2026 publication header, revises correspondence information and author-note markings, removes the internship footnote, and adds the code sentence. The scientific prose and section and appendix sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reduced in size, Figure 2 moves to an earlier page, and Table 2 and Figure 3 exchange their display order. Front-matter spacing and pagination change, and Table 11's caption label changes from green to black. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The new project-code link modestly improves access and reproducibility documentation. The scientific arguments, experiments, and appendix evidence remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
